description_full: Monarch Casino & Resort, Inc., through its subsidiaries, owns and operates hotels and casinos. It owns and operates hotels and casinos under the Atlantis Casino Resort Spa in Reno, Nevada and the Monarch Casino Resort Spa Black Hawk in Black Hawk, Colorado. The company also owns separate parcels of land. In addition, it owns and operates The Toucan Charlie's Buffet & Grille, which offers a variety of food selections; The Atlantis Steakhouse, a fine dining destination; The Bistro Napa, which features wine country cuisine; The Oyster Bar on the Sky Terrace, which offers pan roasts made-to-order, fresh seafood, cioppino, house made chowder, and bisques; Sushi Bar, which serves sushi rolls; The Purple Parrot coffee shop, which serves breakfast and American comfort food; The Red Bloom Asian kitchen, which offers Asian dishes; The Manhattan Deli, which offers matzo ball soup, piled high sandwiches, salads, house made soups, bagels and lox, New York style pizza, and New York cheesecake; and The Chicago Dogs Eatery, a snack bar that serves Chicago-style hot dogs, pizza, ice cream, and arcade-style refreshments, as well as two gourmet coffee bars that offer coffee drinks, sandwiches, house made gelato, and freshly baked pastries. Monarch Casino & Resort, Inc. was incorporated in 1993 and is based in Reno, Nevada.

financial_summary: Monarch Casino & Resort, Inc. is a small-cap consumer cyclical business with a $1.9B market cap on $545M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 17% against a 9% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, and 20% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $128M in free cash flow — roughly 24 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.62× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -8.9% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.0× net debt/EBITDA.

Shareholder yield of 4.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 33% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
